patch_description: The key weakness is the blind hill-climbing: it perturbs random points and immediately accepts any score increase, which gets stuck easily. Improvement strategy based on Heilbronn-specific geometric insight: the objective is governed by a few "bottleneck" triangles, so moves should target vertices of the currently-smallest triangles. I also improve seeds (12-gon + center, two-ring 7+6 configuration are classic boundary-heavy Heilbronn candidates), use simulated annealing with reheating to escape local optima, always track the global best, and use a scale-invariant step size (sigma scaled by hull diameter) so moves don't stall for small/large configurations. Targeted edits to the seed construction and the optimization loop.
